core_message: An island sat on maps and Google Earth for over a century, and it had never existed.
title: Why Did Maps Show a Fake Island?
description:
Sandy Island appeared on charts of the Coral Sea, between Australia and New Caledonia, after a whaling ship reported it in 1876. It stayed on maps for over a century, Google Earth included.

In November 2012 an Australian research ship, the Southern Surveyor, sailed to the spot. There was only open ocean, about 1,400 metres deep. 3D scenes made in Blender with CC0 assets by Kenney and Quaternius.
comment_question: What other place on a map do you think isn't really there?

scenes.narration: In 2012, scientists sailed to this exact spot to find an island. There was nothing here but open ocean.
scenes.purpose: the island on the maps isn't there

scenes.narration: The island first appeared in 1876, when a whaling ship called the Velocity reported sandy islets here, in the Coral Sea.
For more than a century, Sandy Island sat on charts and atlases, and even on Google Earth, between Australia and New Caledonia.
scenes.purpose: it stayed on maps for a century

scenes.narration: So when an Australian research ship, the Southern Surveyor, passed nearby, its scientists went to take a look.
Their echo sounder found no island at all. The sea floor was fourteen hundred metres down.
scenes.purpose: deep ocean where the island should be

scenes.narration: Sandy Island never existed. The ship had sailed straight across it.
